coreIdea: Chomsky hierarchy: Regular ⊊ DCFL ⊊ CFL ⊊ CSL ⊊ Recursive ⊊ RE ⊊ all. Test bottom-up: Regular? → CFL? → Recursive/RE (via Decidability tools).
mustRememberFormulas: Canonical examples: a*b*=Regular, a^nb^n=CFL-not-Regular, a^nb^nc^n=CSL-not-CFL, Halting-style=RE-not-Recursive
Recursive closed under complement; RE(not-recursive) is NOT closed under complement
CFL∩CFL: NO guarantee (can escape CFL entirely); Regular+anything stays at the other's level
Bounded/constant tape or stack size → collapses to Regular power

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: single language given, asked which hierarchy level
multiple languages combined via ∪/∩/complement, asked resulting class
general closure TRUE/FALSE claim across hierarchy levels
restricted machine model (bounded tape/stack), asked equivalent class

commonTrapsQuickList: CFL∩CFL has NO safety guarantee — can jump straight to CSL or beyond
RE is NOT closed under complement (only Recursive is) — the crux of Recursive-vs-RE
A CONSTANT-bounded stack/tape always collapses power to Regular
Real programming languages (FORTRAN etc.) are typically context-sensitive, not context-free
highYieldPyqLessons: Combined-classification via set operations (14/31) is the biggest sub-skill — memorize the closure-rule table across all levels, with CFL∩CFL as the standout exception.
This topic is the true test of whether Regular Language + CFL + Decidability are ALL solid — treat it as the final integration checkpoint for TOC.
